correctness.rationale: A common two-deletion output is precisely a size-three submultiset of the coordinatewise minimum; it exists iff the sum of those minima is at least three. On weight five, this is equivalent to a full ℓ₁ separation of less than six. An independent deletion-shadow replay checked the ten-word witness, reconstructed all 126 profiles and verified the printed case minima and incidences. A and B have a fixed common size-three submultiset and C has pairwise overlap at least three by the verified table and coordinate symmetry. Pointwise coverage is 16a+3b+c≥16, and the summed clique weights are exactly 5+20(3/16)+20(1/16)=10, proving the bound. Independent short proof: remove every word with some count ≥3 (at most one per symbol, and never two such counts in a single word), then insert all five pure words with no size loss and no conflict with the residual words. If a,b,c are the residual counts of types 221, 2111 and 11111, their disjoint size-three output sets use 4a+3b≤20 outputs with a double symbol and a+3b+10c≤10 all-distinct outputs. Twice the first plus the second gives 9a+9b+10c≤50, so at most five residual words coexist. The construction has five, hence 10 is exact.
residual_risks: The result is finite and complete for these parameters only. It is not a classification of optimal codes and does not apply to ordered deletion or binary constant-weight codes.

value.rationale: This determines an exact quinary benchmark in the studied t=n−3 multiset regime and the first weight outside the cited unbounded weight-at-most-four results. The lower construction establishes that the general upper benchmark is attainable at these parameters; attainment with disjoint typed deletion shadows is not supplied by a size bound alone. The result gives a compact test instance for exact ℓ₁ and multiset-code bounds. Value is for the exact two-deletion capacity and witness, not for the generic clique-cover technique or for giving a second derivation of an upper bound.
residual_risks: The scientific increment is a single exact finite parameter; no optimal-code census, extension or new general packing theorem has been claimed.
